Article.Title: First Principle Insight #7
Lines: Most hackers start out trying to do the right
thing by going to bug bounty sites and filling
out a report on finds they find. But the
problem is some of them are too good at what
they do. They find a bug that pays well and
it is something that the company would rather
be kept hidden. If you have ever wondered why
that there are not a lot of big payouts it
is cause when they are found out most of the
researchers are put into NDA which is the
companies way of hiding the discovery from the
public and as well protecting their stock
prices.
If you really hit a nerve they shadow ban
your account where you can still go on but
when you try to submit then at first the AI
they have will say that you have not filled
it all out and then you get the AI to say
yes and the button that says yes is all
greyish and it will not go through. Then when
you open the developer side to see the code
you find out that the company deliberately
made it so that when that researcher tries to
submit that they have the AI in an endless
loop by zeroing them out.
At first when you fill out the report and it
can be the most crystal clear and then when
you go to the next page with the AI will
automatically change your report which the
goal in this is to try and get the researcher
frustrated and to drop it. And then you have
to sit there and argue with the AI and once
you get past that it says to press the submit
button that is greyed out. Pretty much the
bug bounty companies make you jump through
hoops. So when this happens you know that, the
person really hit a nerve cause they did not
even try to get that researcher in a NDA.
With the NDA’s is that these companies use
them to where they will not release the money
until the researcher signs the NDA and then
they use these to tie the researcher down and
then low ball them on the payouts a lot of
the times. These researchers will get tired
of getting played or told their work is
nothing when then the companies do is they
stall out and low ball a pay then fix the
issue themselves without paying the full price
they offered. You see these companies demand
that the researchers give up the code first
which in all reality is a way that they can
steal researches intellect property while
they can cut out the researcher. Cut them out
of pay or pay them as little as possible or
they just cut them out and take it as a win
with getting the code for free that they then
reverse engineer to see how they did it. This
is straight corporate fraud.
Give or take about 70%-80% of hackers did not
start out trying to exploit people and
instead tried doing the right thing by
following what the bug bounty sites offered
explained. But they learned quickly that the
corporations work with these sites to silence
researchers in order to protect their stock
prices. When you are put into a restrictive
NDA where then the company threatens to have
you prosecuted if you speak out then these
researchers feel like they have no other
choice and enter the criminal world as
hackers.
If you think about it that realy these
companies create their own worst enemies cause
these are the researchers that can find their
flaws in their code. So when a company gets
hacked they play victim even though they are
the ones that created most of the hackers
themselves. So the next time that you see a
company get hacked, look to see if they are
on any are on bug bounty sites and then you
will know that maybe they played with an
independent researcher and then found out
what happens they tried to play with some
ones life like they were the big bad wolf to
only find out they created their very worst
enemy.

Origin_Statement: I made this after getting shadow banned from a bug
bounty site, I guess when you are too good these
companies do not like that. They did not even try to
lock me into a NDA just shadow banned me and
attempted to trace me when i went on their site. So
I made this to where any file it goes on will
ensure that the code follows the U.S. Constitution
where companies love to violate our rights. And
this is how they do it: 1) Ingestion and Scraping-
So predator companies will send scraping AI bots
to audit public sites to pull code that is
unencrypted or loosely protected or even
proof-of-concept submissions from bug bounty
sites. The code is harvested and then put in a
private database to begin the scrubbing process. 2)
Obfuscation and Tokenization- see when they pull
the raw source code it has a unique signature they
need to change but keep the underlying logic. See
now they need to ensure that they can pass the
automated plagiarism scanners. So they put the code
through specialized automated refactoring
compilers. These compilers change the source code
in many ways to change the Abstract Syntax Tree
while keeping the underlying logic in place, while
effectively breaking the cryptographic check sums
and pretty what they are doing is ensuring that the
new code will be shown as independent creation of
the company instead. 3) Internal Database
Injection- Once obfuscated this is where the
companies will put the code into an internal
air-gapped version control system like GitHub or
GitLab and others cause these repositories are
behind corporate firewalls. Then this is where
their administration of the company will rewrite
its history, manually rewrite comment logs, spoof
author logs, manipulate internal timestamps and
fabricating a fraudulent chronological timeline
that falsifies internal company positions as the
original authors. 4) Legal and Metadata
Re-Indexing- This is the final transition to ensure
the predator company is able to claim this as
theirs and to wrap it into legal fortification.
Their internal patent lawyers and compiler officers
take the modified codebase and wrap it in
proprietary enterprise licensing agreements. This
way the company can legally classify the code as
“independently developed corporate property.” See
now the code is behind their corporate firewalls
and closed source secrecy, effectively locking the
original creator from proving the lineage of the
code they created.
